# Magic Bag restructure: rarities, collection unlocks and the Mythic Omni Bag (build spec)

*Written 2026-09-25 by the research workflow (bag restructure). Research only: no build script, patch script, mod folder, save or game file was changed.*
*Builds on the LIVE pins in `tools/deploy_set.py`: **SkyySacks 0.7.6** (`SkyySacks/build_skyysacks_0.7.6.py`, generated by `tools/sacks_0_7_6_patch.py`) and **SkyyCollections 0.2.2** (`SkyyCollections/build_skyycollections_0.2.2.py`, generated by `tools/coll_0_2_2_patch.py`). Targets: **SkyySacks 0.8.0** (new `tools/sacks_0_8_0_patch.py`) and **SkyyCollections 0.2.3** (new `tools/coll_0_2_3_patch.py`), deployed together. Edit the patch scripts, never the generated files.*
*Does not touch SkyyGear, SkyyAuctions, SkyyMenu or SkyyRolls (another workflow owns them). Adds no stat modifiers, so no modifier key can clash with SkyyGear's.*

**Skyy's calls.**
- HANDOFF section 1, Exploration rules: "each bag's main expansion will come from a collection in its field (e.g. Mining bag per Iron tier), Exploration gives slight boosts - a later bag restructure". Same in `docs/plans/SkyyExploration-Plan.md` answer 4.
- `docs/plans/SkyWynn-Decisions.md` change notes 2026-09-25 #7 (e): **Mining bag upgrades come from the Iron collection.**
- Change note #8: **bags use rarities, not sizes.** Normal, Unique, Rare, Legendary replace Small / Medium / Large. A **Mythic Omni Bag** combines all the Legendary bags. It holds **100,000 of each item for every bag type**, keeps each bag type on its own tab, and is the only bag you need to carry.

**Legend.** VERIFIED = seen in `HytaleServer.jar` bytecode (tools/dev and a scratch copy of its bytecode printer), in `Assets.zip` (read in memory), in our build scripts, in Skyy's save or in a server log (read-only). UNVERIFIED = design, inference or not yet tested in game. `[SKYY?]` = a default for Skyy (they/them) to confirm.

---

## 0. Summary

**"We have Mining, Foraging, Farming, Combat and Smithing bags, right?"** Yes. SkyySacks 0.7.5 added the Smithing bag, and the live 0.7.6 has five bag types. Each type has Small, Medium and Large, so there are 15 bag items today, all free Workbench recipes. VERIFIED (`BAG_CATS` in `build_skyysacks_0.7.6.py`).

What this spec decides:

1. **Collection per bag.** The rule: a bag grows from a collection whose items that same bag holds.
   - Mining: **Iron Ore** (locked by Skyy).
   - Foraging: **Oak Log**.
   - Farming: **Wheat**.
   - Combat: **Bone Fragments**.
   - Smithing (new): **Light Hide**.
   No collection feeds two bags. The four non-Mining picks are defaults `[SKYY?]`.
2. **One unlock ladder for every bag.** Normal at tier I, Unique at III, Rare at V, Legendary at VII. That is 50 / 250 / 1,000 / 5,000 items on all five collections (section 2.3 explains why, not Iron III/V/VIII).
3. **Tiers and per-item caps.**

   | Tier | Id | Cap per item |
   |---|---|---|
   | Normal | `_Small` | 640 |
   | Unique | `_Medium` | 2,240 |
   | Rare (new) | `_Rare` | **6,720** |
   | Legendary | `_Large` | 20,160 |
   | Mythic Omni (new) | `Skyy_Sack_Omni` | 100,000 of every item of every bag type |

   Owners keep every number they have. All five caps are editable in Server Setup.
4. **Ids stay.** `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Small|Medium|Large` keep working, with new names and a new quality. New ids are `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Rare` and `Skyy_Sack_Omni`. SkyySacks gets five item qualities of its own (`Skyy_Bag_Normal` ... `Skyy_Bag_Mythic`) in the Wynn colours.
5. **The unlock is the engine's own recipe knowledge.** VERIFIED: a `KnowledgeRequired` recipe cannot be crafted at a real bench unless the player knows its output item.
   - SkyySacks marks the 20 tiered bag recipes `KnowledgeRequired: true`.
   - It teaches and forgets them from SkyyCollections' `coll:recipes:<uuid>`.
   - The /craft Collections tab keeps crafting unlocked recipes without a bench.
6. **The Omni.** Recipe: one Legendary bag of each of the five types at a Workbench. No collection gate. It wins for every type, and the bag page shows all five tabs at 100,000.
7. **Coin-bypass.** A bought tier never unlocks a bag above **Unique**. This is a new SkyyCollections setting, `bypass.bagMax`.
8. **Admin override.** SkyySacks gets `bags.freeRecipes`, default off, which gives the old free recipes. The same happens automatically when SkyyCollections is not installed, because SkyySacks must stay standalone.
9. **Migration.**
   - Owned bags keep working.
   - Their saved quality is restamped as players carry them.
   - Untouched `rewards.properties` bag lines move to the new ladder by themselves.
   - Players already past a tier get the unlock at once: the unlock list is recomputed from counts on every publish.
10. **Found while reading** (section 12): the /craft page ignores `KnowledgeRequired` on 19 vanilla recipes. Saved bag stacks carry their own quality index. `caps()` accepts unknown tier words.

### 1.2 SkyyCollections 0.2.2 (VERIFIED, `build_skyycollections_0.2.2.py`)

- **Bag rewards in the default `rewards.properties`** (the `BAG` lambda). There are 11 lines, each with a single token:
  - `Wheat.5` Medium Farming, `Wheat.8` Large Farming. Wheat has no Small row, because Small was free.
  - `OakLog.3/5/8` Small / Medium / Large Foraging.
  - `Cobblestone.3/5/8` Small / Medium / Large Mining.
  - `Bone.3/5/8` Small / Medium / Large Combat.
  - No Smithing rows.
- **Recipe ids `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_<Tier>_Recipe_Generated_0` resolve.** VERIFIED in Skyy's server log `2026-09-25_05-24-41_server.log`: "28 recipe unlock(s)" with no "unknown recipe id(s) skipped" line. The 28 include all 11 bag ids, since `validate()` counts only ids found in `CraftingRecipe.getAssetMap()`. This closes the `research/Collections-Spec.md` 4.3 note that the pattern was unverified for Skyy items.
- These unlocks do nothing today, because every bag is also a free Workbench recipe (the Collections-Spec 4.3 follow-up).
- **Unlock list.** `CollUnlocks.compute(d)` walks every visible collection. For tiers 1 up to `effTier = max(count tier, bought tier)` it adds `recipesAt(c, t)`. It republishes `coll:recipes:<uuid>` on every tier change, purchase, epoch or profile switch.
- **Coin-bypass.** The shipped walls are `bypass.walls=5,4,3,0` (Bulk V, Standard IV, Rare III, Elite never). A purchase buys the next tier's recipe unlocks only.
- **Names.** `CollUtil.prettyItem` prints `Skyy_Sack_Mining_Small` as "Small Mining Bag".
- **Bridge.** It publishes `coll:recipes:<uuid>`, `coll:fn:count`, `coll:fn:tier`, `coll:fn:add` and `coll:list`. `coll:fn:tier` is published in `setup()` and removed only in `shutdown()`.

### 1.3 Engine: per-player recipe knowledge (VERIFIED bytecode)

- **The flag.** `CraftingRecipe.isKnowledgeRequired()` is read from `"KnowledgeRequired"` in an item's `Recipe` block. Only Crafting-type recipes may set it: the codec says "KnowledgeRequired in recipe can't be set for non crafting recipes". The bag recipes are `Type: Crafting` (Workbench).
- **The check.** `CraftingManager.isValidBenchForRecipe` takes the recipe's **primary output item id**. If the recipe needs knowledge and `Player.getPlayerConfigData().getKnownRecipes()` lacks that id, it logs "Attempted to craft %s but doesn't know the recipe!" and returns false.
  - `craftItem` and `queueCraft` both call it, so every real bench craft is checked.
- **Teaching and forgetting.** `CraftingPlugin.learnRecipe(Ref, String itemId, ComponentAccessor)` and `forgetRecipe` are `public static`. They copy the set, `setKnownRecipes(...)`, then call `sendKnownRecipes(Ref, ComponentAccessor)`.
  - That sends `UpdateKnownRecipes`, mapping every known item id to its recipes. Unknown item ids are skipped.
  - `CraftingPlugin$PlayerAddedSystem` sends it again whenever the player entity is added (join and every world switch).
- **Storage.** `Store` implements `ComponentAccessor`, so SkyySacks' `SweepTask` can pass its `st`.
  - The set is saved **per player**, not per profile: `"KnownRecipes": []` sits in Skyy's `universe/players/<uuid>.json`.
  - No Skyy mod reads or writes it today (grep over every build script).
- **Vanilla use.** It sets `KnowledgeRequired: true` on 19 recipes: Bronze, Bronze Ornate, Leather Raven and Steel Ancient armor, three pies and Caesar salad.
- UNVERIFIED: how the client draws a knowledge recipe the player does not know at a bench (hidden or greyed). Also unverified: whether an **open** bench refreshes when `UpdateKnownRecipes` arrives (test T3).

### 1.4 Item qualities (VERIFIED)

- **Vanilla.** `Server/Item/Qualities/*.json`: Common `#c9d2dd` (value 1), Uncommon `#3e9049` (2), Rare `#2770b7` (3), Epic `#8b339e` (4), Legendary `#bb8a2c` (5), plus technical ones (Template 10). Each JSON names its tooltip and slot textures under `UI/ItemQualities/...`.
- **Mods ship their own.** VERIFIED: `AssetRegistryLoader` loads the `Item/Qualities` asset path.
  - SkyyVault 0.1.2 ships `SkyyVaultButton` (lang `general.qualities.<Id>` plus the `server.` twin).
  - 13 other jars and zips in Skyy's Mods folders ship their own.
  - Two of them use the bare names `Mythic` (Extended Backpacks) and `Mythos` (Skyys-Modpack). **Never use a bare rarity word as an id.**
  - UNVERIFIED in game: that a plugin pack's quality shows on its items (test T1; SkyyGear's spec has the same open test).
  - Fallback if it does not: the rarity is still in every bag's name, and the bag page draws its own colours, so only the tooltip frame and colour are lost.
- **Saved stacks carry their quality index.** VERIFIED:
  - `ItemStack` has a `qualityIndex` field (`Integer.MIN_VALUE` = "use the item's quality") and a `Quality` codec key.
  - Skyy's save stores `"Quality": 5` on every Large bag. 5 is the index of Rare (Cobalt armor, asset quality Rare, is also saved as 5).
  - So changing a bag's asset quality does **not** change bags already in inventories. They must be restamped (section 5.6).
- **Indexes follow load order.** `IndexedLookupTableAssetMap` hands out indexes from a counter as assets load. That is why mod qualities are not stable numbers across installs.
- **Quality value limit.** SkyyAuctions 0.1.1 treats quality value >= 8 as a technical item that cannot be traded (`AhItem.technical`). Bag qualities must stay below 8.

## 2. Which collection grows each bag

### 2.1 Rule

A bag's collection must be one whose items **that same bag holds**: `SackDefs.catOf(item) == bag type`. This is the plain meaning of "a collection in its field", because the bags define the fields. It also keeps the unlock where the player already is: filling a Mining bag with iron ore is what raises the Iron collection. Other rules:
- No collection feeds two bags.
- No mob family feeds two bag collections.
- Collections are per profile, so unlocks are per profile.

### 2.2 The five collections

| Bag | Collection (id, curve) | `catOf` check | Why | Alternatives `[SKYY?]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mining | **Iron Ore** (`Iron`, Standard) | `Ore_Iron` -> Mining | Skyy's lock (change note 7e). Iron is the second metal, the SkyBlock-style "signature" mining material | - |
| Foraging | **Oak Log** (`OakLog`, Bulk) | `Wood_Oak_Trunk` -> Foraging | The live default and SkyBlock's own choice. The most common log: Oak, Apple trunks, ferns and felled logs all count | Stick (Bulk: bushes and branches everywhere) |
| Farming | **Wheat** (`Wheat`, Standard) | `Plant_Crop_Wheat_Item` -> Farming | The live default and SkyBlock's Farming sack line (Wheat II/V/VIII/X) | Essence of Life (Bulk: every ripe crop gives 2-4, so any farming style counts) |
| Combat | **Bone Fragments** (`Bone`, Standard) | `Ingredient_Bone_Fragment` -> Combat | The live default. 32 undead roles | - |
| Smithing | **Light Hide** (`HideLight`, Standard) | `Ingredient_Hide_Light` -> Smithing (hides moved there in 0.7.5) | Hides become leather at the Tannery, and the Normal Smithing Bag itself takes Light Leather. Comes from 35 common animals (chicken, deer, antelope, camel), not the undead that feed Bone | Linen Scraps (same skeletons as Bone, so rejected). Copper Ore (fails the rule: the Mining bag holds ore) |

Notes:
- Light Hide is a **Combat-category** collection in the SkyyCollections registry, so the Smithing bag's rewards show on a Combat collection page. Combat collections pay double coins instead of skill XP (unchanged).
- Cobblestone loses its bag rows and keeps Copper Pickaxe (I), Stone Brick (IV) and Iron Pickaxe (VI).

### 2.3 The ladder: Normal I, Unique III, Rare V, Legendary VII (all five bags)

| Rarity | Tier | Items (Bulk and Standard share thresholds up to VIII) | That tier's default rewards (Collections-Spec 4.2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal | I | 50 | +50 coins |
| Unique | III | 250 | +200 coins, +500 skill XP (Combat: 400 coins) |
| Rare | V | 1,000 | +800 coins, +2,500 skill XP (Combat: 1,600 coins) |
| Legendary | VII | 5,000 | +3,000 coins, +10,000 skill XP (Combat: 6,000 coins) |

Why this ladder and not a straight move to Iron III/V/VIII:
- **Normal must stay early.** It was a free recipe until now. At Iron III (250 iron ore) new players would lose their first Mining bag for a long time.
  - Tier I is the earliest tier: 50 items.
  - Coins can also buy it once one iron ore is found. At neutral Bazaar demand that is 49 missing x 9 coins (Iron Ore instant buy) x 5 = **2,205 coins**, and new profiles start with 10,000.
  - The old Cobblestone III point (250 cobble) is about when a player finds their first iron, so the early pace barely changes. UNVERIFIED ratio.
- **Two tiers between steps.** This matches the live III/V/VIII spacing and SkyBlock's sack ladders (Mining sack at Coal V/VII/IX; Wheat II/V/VIII/X).
- **Legendary at VII, not VIII.**
  - VII is the curve's big milestone (+10,000 XP).
  - The Mythic Omni needs **five** Legendary bags, so each Legendary must land in mid-late game, not at the end of five separate lines.
  - VIII and IX stay free for later prestige rewards: minions, bag perks, Exploration boosts.
  - Iron VIII would be 10,000 iron ore with no fortune stat yet. Collections-Spec 4.1 already notes the top tiers are 1/2-1/8 of SkyBlock's.
- **One rule players can learn.** Bulk and Standard have the same thresholds through tier VIII, so the ladder gives identical numbers on all five collections.
- **Coin-bypass fit.** With the shipped walls, coins can buy the Normal and Unique tiers (early game). Rare and Legendary must be gathered, which section 7 enforces for Bulk too.
- Iron may feel slower than logs or wheat at the same numbers. Each bag's rows are plain `rewards.properties` lines, so one collection can move without code `[SKYY?]`.

## 3. The rarity ladder (per bag type)

### 3.1 Items, caps, recipes, unlocks

| Rarity | Item id | Display name | Quality | Cap key (default) | Recipe (Workbench, `Workbench_Crafting`) | Knowledge | Unlocked at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal | `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Small` (kept) | Normal `<Type>` Bag | `Skyy_Bag_Normal` | `bag.small` (640) | 3 Bolt of Wool + 4 `BAG_MAT` (unchanged) | required | collection tier I |
| Unique | `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Medium` (kept) | Unique `<Type>` Bag | `Skyy_Bag_Unique` | `bag.medium` (2,240) | Normal bag + 6 Linen Scraps (`Ingredient_Fabric_Scrap_Linen`; changed: was 3 Bolt of Linen) | required | tier III |
| Rare | `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Rare` (**new**) | Rare `<Type>` Bag | `Skyy_Bag_Rare` | `bag.rare` (**6,720**) | Unique bag + 6 Shadoweave Scraps (`Ingredient_Fabric_Scrap_Shadoweave`) | required | tier V |
| Legendary | `Skyy_Sack_<Type>_Large` (kept) | Legendary `<Type>` Bag | `Skyy_Bag_Legendary` | `bag.large` (20,160) | **Rare** bag + 6 Cindercloth Scraps (`Ingredient_Fabric_Scrap_Cindercloth`; changed: was Medium + 3 Bolt of Silk) | required | tier VII |
| Mythic | `Skyy_Sack_Omni` (**new**) | Mythic Omni Bag | `Skyy_Bag_Mythic` | `bag.omni` (**100,000**, every type) | 1 Legendary bag of each type (section 4) | **not** required | none (owning the 5 bags) |

- **Rare cap 6,720 = 3 x 2,240 = 20,160 / 3.** It is the exact geometric middle of Unique and Legendary: sqrt(2,240 x 20,160) = 6,720. Each step up gives about three times the room.
- **Existing owners stay whole.** Small, Medium and Large keep 640 / 2,240 / 20,160 as Normal / Unique / Legendary.
- **The next rarity needs the previous one**, like accessories (change note 17). So Legendary now takes a Rare bag. A Large recipe of "Medium + Silk" would skip the new tier.
- **Upgrade materials = mob-dropped fabric scraps** (review fix, 2026-09-28). The first draft used Bolt of Linen / Silk / Cindercloth, but those come only from the Loombench, whose recipe needs 3 Cotton Scraps (`Ingredient_Fabric_Scrap_Cotton`) that no drop table gives, and from salvaging cloth armor that itself needs those bolts and never drops (VERIFIED `Assets.zip`). The live 0.7.6 Medium / Large recipes have the same problem. The scraps follow the vanilla armor tiers and are already Smithing-bag items: **Linen Scraps** (goblins, trorks: 41 NPC drop tables), **Shadoweave Scraps** (outlanders: 9), **Cindercloth Scraps** (burnt skeletons, Incandescent skeletons, fire dragon, flame golem, wraith: 14). Silk Scraps are not used: nothing drops them. Normal keeps 3 Bolt of Wool (Wool Scraps drop from sheep, Furniture Bench). The build stops if a step material is no longer dropped by an NPC (or one recipe step from one). **The 6 per step is a PLACEHOLDER** `[SKYY?]`.
- **Twenty knowledge-gated recipes** (5 types x 4 rarities) plus one ungated Omni recipe. 21 item JSONs, 5 quality JSONs.

### 3.2 Rarity look: own qualities in the Wynn colours

The rarity names and colours are the Wynn ladder of change note 5: Normal white, Unique yellow, Rare pink, Legendary aqua, Mythic purple. Hex values are Wynncraft's own chat colours.

| Quality id | Label | TextColor (tooltip) | Page text colour | QualityValue | Vanilla textures reused (by hue) | Drop particle (SkyyGear's, by hue) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Skyy_Bag_Normal` | Normal | `#ffffff` | `#ffffff` | 1 | Common | `Drop_Common` |
| `Skyy_Bag_Unique` | Unique | `#ffff55` | `#ffff55` | 2 | Legendary (gold frame reads as yellow) | `Drop_Legendary` |
| `Skyy_Bag_Rare` | Rare | `#ff55ff` | `#ff55ff` | 3 | Epic (purple frame reads as pink) | `Drop_Epic` |
| `Skyy_Bag_Legendary` | Legendary | `#55ffff` | `#55ffff` | 4 | Rare (blue frame reads as aqua) | `Drop_Rare` |
| `Skyy_Bag_Mythic` | Mythic | `#aa00aa` | **`#cc66cc`** | 6 | Epic | `Drop_Epic` |

- **JSON shape.** Each JSON copies the vanilla shape and texture paths exactly (`UI/ItemQualities/Tooltips/ItemTooltip<X>.png`, `...Arrow.png`, `UI/ItemQualities/Slots/Slot<X>.png` for Slot, BlockSlot and SpecialSlot). Other fields: `LocalizationKey: server.general.qualities.<Id>`, `VisibleQualityLabel: true`, `RenderSpecialSlot: true`, `ItemEntityConfig.ParticleSystemId`. Lang writes both `general.qualities.<Id>=<Label>` and the `server.` twin (the SkyyVault pattern).
- **Matches SkyyGear exactly.** VERIFIED against `research/SkyyGear-Stage1-Spec.md` 2.1 (written the same day for the SkyyGear build): the same hexes, the same frame art by hue (Unique = Legendary frame, Rare = Epic, Legendary = Rare, Mythic = Epic) and the same QualityValue 1-6. The drop particles are SkyyGear's too (`SkyyGear/build_skyygear_0.1.py` `RARITIES`, by hue like the frame: Normal `Drop_Common`, Unique `Drop_Legendary`, Rare `Drop_Epic`, Legendary `Drop_Rare`, Mythic `Drop_Epic`; review fix 2026-09-28, was one particle per rank).
- **Ids are SkyySacks-owned** (`Skyy_Bag_` prefix, unused in the repo). SkyyGear ships `Skyy_Gear_<Name>`. Two packs defining one asset id would depend on load order, so the ids must differ. Only the look is shared.
- **Build-time look check.** If a `SkyyGear/build_skyygear_*.py` exists, the SkyySacks build reads its newest copy as text and parses its `RARITIES` tuples (`(id, name, hex, page hex, tooltip frame, slot frame, drop particle)`). For the four shared rarities plus Mythic it compares the tooltip hex, the frame art and the drop particle, and stops on a mismatch, so a Unique bag and Unique gear look and glow the same. A script that is missing, unreadable or mid-edit falls back to the SkyyGear spec 2.1 table (hexes only, it has no particle column) with a printed note; an unreadable source never stops the build. It never imports the script. This is the `_camp_defaults_check` pattern. SkyyGear owns the rarity look: if it picks other hexes, texture mapping or particles, SkyySacks follows.
- **Mythic on the page.** `#aa00aa` on the page background `#0b1524` is contrast 2.9:1, too dark for big readable text. The bag page draws Mythic text in `#cc66cc` (about 5.5:1). The item tooltip keeps `#aa00aa` to match Wynn and SkyyGear `[SKYY?]`.
- QualityValue stays below 8 (SkyyAuctions' technical threshold, 1.4).

## 4. The Mythic Omni Bag

| Point | Decision |
|---|---|
| Recipe | `Skyy_Sack_Omni` = 1 each of `Skyy_Sack_Mining_Large`, `_Foraging_Large`, `_Farming_Large`, `_Combat_Large`, `_Smithing_Large`. Workbench, `Workbench_Crafting`, no tier level, `KnowledgeRequired: false`. Recipe id `Skyy_Sack_Omni_Recipe_Generated_0` |
| Collection gate | **None** beyond owning the five Legendary bags (each already needs its own tier VII) `[SKYY?]` |
| Where it crafts | Any real Workbench (visible to everyone, since no knowledge is needed). The /craft Crafting tab while a Workbench accessory is equipped. **Also the /craft Collections tab whenever the player carries all five Legendary bags**: SkyySacks adds the Omni recipe to that tab's list itself, so it is inventory-craftable like the other bags (end state in HANDOFF: "everything is inventory crafting") |
| What it does | In `caps(inv)`, `Skyy_Sack_Omni` gives `CAP_OMNI` to **every** type in `SackDefs.CATS` (including a later sixth type such as Fishing, with no change) |
| Best bag | Highest cap per type wins (today's rule, unchanged). With the defaults, and whenever the order check (section 8.1) is respected, that is always the Omni: 100,000 > 20,160 |
| Contents | Nothing to move. The pool is per profile and keyed by item id, so combining bags loses nothing, and a player who drops the Omni keeps every pooled item (strict access as today) |
| Right-click | Opens page id `SkyySacks` (the existing no-type factory), so the default tab rule picks a type with items |
| Trading | Like every bag today (section 13, question 7) |

## 5. SkyySacks 0.8.0: how an unlock reaches players

### 5.1 Asset changes

- One bag table (the 0.7.5 single-source rule) grows a tier list: `(suffix, rarity, quality id, cap key, previous suffix, bolt id, bolt qty)` for Small / Medium / Rare / Large, plus the Omni row. It feeds:
  - the 21 item JSONs, the 5 quality JSONs and the lang;
  - `SackDefs` arrays: `TIERS = {Small, Medium, Rare, Large}`, `RAR_NAME = {Normal, Unique, Rare, Legendary, Mythic}`, `RAR_COLOR` (tooltip hexes), `RAR_PAGE` (page hexes), `OMNI = "Skyy_Sack_Omni"`;
  - the bag page texts.
- `sack_item(...)` gains `"KnowledgeRequired": true` inside `Recipe` for the 20 tiered bags and `false` for the Omni.
- `BAG_CATS`, `catOf` and every sweep and pool rule stay as they are.

### 5.2 Knowledge sync (new class `KnowSync`, compiled before `SweepTask`)

- `MANAGED` = the 20 tiered bag item ids, generated from the table. SkyySacks owns these entries in every player's known set and never touches any other entry.
- `free()` = `SackCfg.FREE_RECIPES || !(bridge().get("coll:fn:tier") instanceof java.util.function.Function)`. Free when the admin says so, or when SkyyCollections is not installed. Every plugin's `setup()` runs before the first 2 s tick, so this read is stable.
- `wanted(u)`:
  - If `free()`, return all of `MANAGED`.
  - Otherwise read `coll:recipes:<uuid>`. **Absent** means SkyyCollections has not published this player yet, so return `null` and change nothing. An **empty string** means no unlocks.
  - For each listed id that starts with `Skyy_Sack_`, `CraftingRecipe.getAssetMap().getAsset(id).getPrimaryOutput().getItemId()`. Keep it if it is in `MANAGED`.
- `sync(Ref r, Store st, Player p, UUID u)`:
  - Compare `p.getPlayerConfigData().getKnownRecipes().contains(id)` with `wanted.contains(id)` for the 20 ids.
  - On any difference, build `new HashSet(known)`, add and remove only managed ids, then `setKnownRecipes(set)` and **one** `CraftingPlugin.sendKnownRecipes(r, st)`.
  - This is at most 20 set lookups per player every 2 s. A packet goes out only when something changed.
- **Where.** `SweepTask.run()` calls it on the world thread, right after `settledKey(u)` returned a key, before `sweep(...)`.
  - A profile switch therefore re-syncs after the settle window, which already covers the `coll:recipes` republish.
  - Nothing runs on `PlayerReadyEvent`. The engine resends known recipes on every world switch by itself.
- **Side effects.**
  - An admin's vanilla `/recipe learn Skyy_Sack_...` is undone within 2 s. Use `bags.freeRecipes` or `/collections give` instead.
  - Known entries for bags left behind after SkyySacks is removed are harmless: `sendKnownRecipes` skips unknown items (VERIFIED).
- `B.probe` covers `CraftingRecipe.isKnowledgeRequired`, `CraftingRecipe.getPrimaryOutput`, `Player.getPlayerConfigData`, `PlayerConfigData.getKnownRecipes/setKnownRecipes`, `CraftingPlugin.sendKnownRecipes`, `ItemStack.withQuality`, `Item.getQualityIndex` and `ItemContainer.setItemStackForSlot`.

### 5.3 The /craft page

- **Collections tab** (`C:`):
  - Lists `coll:recipes` as today, so every unlocked bag recipe crafts there **without a bench** (materials from inventory and bags).
  - Plus the Omni recipe while the player carries all five Legendary bags (section 4).
  - The tab shows when either list is non-empty.
- **Crafting / Smithing / Farming tabs and search** (the merged set) filter with `recipeAllowed(r, u, known)`:
  - Not `isKnowledgeRequired()`: allowed.
  - A `MANAGED` bag: allowed only if `free()` or its recipe id is in `coll:recipes:<uuid>`. That is the same answer `wanted` gives, so the tab never waits for the 2 s knowledge sync.
  - Any other knowledge recipe (the 19 vanilla ones): allowed only if the player's known set holds its output. This fixes finding 12.1 `[SKYY?]`, default yes.
- **Click time.** The craft click handler runs the same test again before any material moves (a stale page after an unlock change or profile switch). A refused click shows "You have not unlocked this recipe" in the status line.

### 5.4 The bag page

Root grows from 1000 x 600 to **1000 x 630** for the extra lines. The height budgets are below. Element ids have no underscores. Nothing updates on a timer. All dynamic text goes through `b.set`.

**Carried view** (a type with a bag, or any type with the Omni):
- `#SkyySCap` (34 high, 18 bold) is drawn in the best bag's page colour: "Mining - Legendary bag - up to 20,160 of each item - 4,210 stored". With the Omni: "Mining - Mythic Omni Bag - up to 100,000 of each item - 4,210 stored".
- New `#SkyySNext` (26 high, 14) under it, one of:
  - "Next: Rare Mining Bag - Iron Ore tier V (412 / 1,000)", from `coll:fn:where` (section 6.3) for the next rarity's recipe.
  - "Next: Rare Mining Bag - unlocked, craft it at a Workbench or in /craft".
  - For Legendary: "Next: the Mythic Omni Bag - one Legendary bag of each type (you carry 3 of 5)".
  - Omni: "Mythic Omni Bag - every bag type".
  - In free mode the tier text becomes "free on this server".
- Budget: 2 + 46 tabs + 22 grey-tab note (only when some tab is grey, never with the Omni) + 34 + 26 + 4 x 92 grid + 30 info + 48 actions = **576** of 610.

**Not-carried view** (replaces "How to craft one"):
- Title "Mining Bag - you do not carry one yet".
- Holds text.
- "How to get one": the Normal recipe as big icons, unchanged.
- `#SkyySNbStatus` (30 high, 16 bold), one of:
  - "Unlocks at Iron Ore tier I - you have 37 / 50. /collections shows your progress."
  - "Unlocked - craft it at a Workbench, or in /craft -> Collections without a bench."
  - "Free on this server - craft it at a Workbench."
  - "No collection unlocks this bag on this server - ask an admin." (`coll:fn:where` answered `null` without free mode.)
- **Ladder** `#SkyySNbL0..4`: 5 rows of 28 in the rarity page colours. Example: "Normal - 640 of each item - Iron Ore I - UNLOCKED". The Omni row: "Mythic Omni Bag - 100,000 of each item, every bag type - one Legendary bag of each type (you carry 2 of 5)".
- Stored line and info line, as today.
- Hint: "A Workbench can use the materials in the bags you carry. Unlocked bag recipes are also on the Collections tab of /craft."
- Budget: 2 + 46 + 22 + 36 + 62 + 30 + 96 + 30 + 26 header + 140 ladder + 34 + 30 + 44 = **598** of 610.

### 5.5 Best bag: `SweepTask.caps(inv)` and new `best(inv)`

- `id.equals("Skyy_Sack_Omni")`: every type in `CATS` gets `max(current, CAP_OMNI)`.
- Other `Skyy_Sack_` ids: split as today. **Skip** the stack when `SackDefs.catIndex(parts[2]) < 0` or `tierCap(parts[3]) <= 0` (finding 12.2). `tierCap` gains `Rare -> CAP_RARE`.
- `best(inv)` = the same scan returning type -> rarity rank (1-4, 6 for the Omni). It is used only for the page texts and colours.
- Every caller keeps using `caps()`: sweep, withdraw, "Deposit all", the bench link (BagMirror), the craft page's `haveOf`, and the tab states. Carrying only the Omni therefore opens every type everywhere, which is Skyy's "only that one bag".

### 5.6 Restamp saved bag quality (fixes the saved index, 1.4)

- **When.** In the same `SweepTask.run()`, with a settled key only, for each `Skyy_Sack_*` stack in storage, hotbar and backpack whose `getQualityIndex() != getItem().getQualityIndex()`:
  - `cont.setItemStackForSlot(slot, stack.withQuality(stack.getItem().getQualityIndex()))`.
  - `withQuality` keeps id, quantity, durability and metadata (VERIFIED), so only the look changes.
  - Most sweeps find nothing to do.
- **Self-healing.** If another quality mod shifts the index later, the next sweep fixes carried bags again.
- **Bags not carried.** Bags in chests, on the AH, in /trade offers or in SkyyProfiles' inventory snapshots keep the old look until a player carries them. This is cosmetic only: caps come from the id, never from the quality.

### 5.7 Sweep and pooling rules

Unchanged apart from the cap numbers:
- `catOf`, per-item caps per type, the 2 s storage sweep, "Deposit all", the 10 min withdrawal exemption, strict access, and "lowering a cap never deletes items" all stay.
- The per-profile pool files stay.
- Tree sap to Foraging, and hides and fabric scraps to Smithing, stay.

### 5.8 One-time notice (always shown, like "Collections now count items", Settings-Spec 2.3)

- **Text.** On the first settled sweep after 0.8.0, a player who has a pool file or carries a `Skyy_Sack_` item gets one chat line (colour `#e0b060`): "[Bags] Magic Bags now use rarities: Small is Normal, Medium is Unique, Large is Legendary - your bags and everything in them are unchanged. New: Rare bags and the Mythic Omni Bag. Bag recipes now unlock through collections - see /pd."
- **Storage.** It is recorded per player (not per profile) in `Skyy_SkyySacks/notices.properties` (`<uuid>=bags-rarity`), written by the SackSaver thread.
- **Why not the pool file.** A meta key in the pool file would load as an item.

### 6.3 New bridge function `coll:fn:where`

`Function apply(Object[]{UUID player (may be null), String recipeId}) -> String "<CollId>|<Collection name>|<tier>|<threshold>|<count>"`:
- It answers for the **lowest** tier of a visible collection whose validated rewards list that recipe. `count` is the player's real count on the active profile (0 without a player).
- It returns `null` when no collection lists the recipe, before `validate()` ran, or on any error. It never throws.
- Registry names cannot contain `|` (build assert), so the answer is safe to split.
- It is published in `setup()` next to `coll:fn:tier` and removed in `shutdown()`.
- Readers: the SkyySacks bag page. Later, any mod that wants to say where a recipe unlocks.

### 6.4 "Free on this server" note

When the bridge value `sacks:freebags` (published by SkyySacks, section 10) is `Boolean.TRUE`, bag recipe names in reward texts get " (free on this server)". Otherwise nothing changes.

## 7. Coin-bypass

- The shipped walls stay: `bypass.walls=5,4,3,0`. The 2026-09-24 tiered lock is still open (Collections-Spec 4.4).
- **New `bypass.bagMax`** (choice `none|normal|unique|rare|legendary`, default **`unique`**) in `CollUnlocks.compute`:

  ```
  ct = countTier(d, R, c); eff = effTier(d, R, c)
  for t in 1..eff:
    for rid in recipesAt(c, t):
      if t > ct and bagRank(rid) > BYP_BAGMAX: skip   # reached only by buying
      out.add(rid)
  bagRank: Skyy_Sack_*_Small 1, _Medium 2, _Rare 3, _Large 4, Skyy_Sack_Omni 5, anything else 0 (never limited)
  ```

- **Result.** Coins can unlock the Normal and Unique bag of every type once the collection is discovered: tiers I and III sit under every non-Elite wall. The Rare and Legendary bags must be gathered on every curve. Without the setting, Oak Log (Bulk, wall V) would sell its Rare bag while Iron (Standard, wall IV) would not.
- **Page texts.**
  - `CollBypass.unlockText` lists an excluded bag as "Rare Foraging Bag - must be gathered".
  - When a tier's only reward is such a bag, it says so; the purchase still just opens the next tier for buying, as today.
  - In the collection view, a BOUGHT row names the bag with "(gather this tier)".
- A bought tier that later becomes a real count tier unlocks the bag as usual (`effTier` / `_paid` flow unchanged).

## 9. Migration

| What | How |
|---|---|
| **Bags players own** | Nothing moves. Same ids, same pool, same caps (Small = Normal 640, Medium = Unique 2,240, Large = Legendary 20,160). Names change at once (lang). The look changes when carried (restamp, 5.6) |
| **Recipes players had for free** | Gone unless unlocked. Those who were free before the update get every tier they have already passed right away. Everyone else needs tier I of that bag's collection (50 items), or buys it with coins |
| **Players already past a tier** | Get the unlock **at once**. `coll:recipes` is computed from current counts on every publish, and SkyySacks teaches within one 2 s sweep. No per-player file changes |
| **`rewards.properties` on existing worlds** | One-time pass `CollBagMigrate.run()`, below |
| **Coin purchases that pointed at a moved bag** | Not refunded. Listed in `migration-bags.log` so an admin can refund by hand `[SKYY?]` |
| **SkyySacks config** | None needed (8.1) |
| **Recipe knowledge** | Starts empty for everyone (`KnownRecipes: []` in Skyy's save). The first sync fills it |

**`CollBagMigrate.run()`** runs in SkyyCollections 0.2.3 `setup()` **before** `CollReg.loadAll()` and before `CfgPub.start`, so the kit's first read already sees the result. It is plain text work with no asset lookups, so it is safe in `setup()`. It uses only `java.*`, so a bare-JVM test can run it on fixture files (the `tools/skyycfg_test.py` pattern).

- **M0 Guard.** A missing file means nothing to do: the new defaults are written by `loadRewards` as today. A file containing the marker line `# bags: rarity ladder (0.2.3)` is already done.
- **M1 Archive.** Copy the file to `rewards-0.2.properties` next to it, or `rewards-0.2.<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.properties` if that exists. This is the `counts-0.1/` / `unlocks-0.1.properties` precedent.
- **M2 Remove untouched old bag lines.**
  - Normalise each live line: trim, turn `\:` and `\=` into `:` and `=`, compare the key case-insensitively, split the value on commas and trim the tokens.
  - A line equal to one of the 11 old defaults (1.2) is deleted.
  - Any other live line holding a `recipe:Skyy_Sack_` token is **hand-edited**. It is kept, logged, and its bag type(s) are marked admin-managed.
- **M3 Add the new tokens** (6.1), skipping admin-managed types and tokens already present on some live line.
  - If a live line already has that key (for example the untouched `OakLog.1=recipe:Tool_Hatchet_Copper...`), append `,<token>` to it (one line per key, the kit's rule).
  - Otherwise append `<Key>=<token>` under the comment `# Magic Bags (rarity ladder: Normal I, Unique III, Rare V, Legendary VII) - SkyyCollections 0.2.3`.
- **M4 Rewrite the ore-line comments.** Replace the two exact old comment lines `#Iron.3=...Armor_Iron_Hands...` and `#Iron.5=...Armor_Iron_Chest...` with the merged forms (6.1).
- **M5 Write.** Add the marker line and write atomically (`CollIO.writeText`). Log every action to `Skyy_SkyyCollections/migration-bags.log`, plus one INFO line: "[SkyyCollections] bag rewards moved to the rarity ladder: N removed, M added, K hand-edited lines kept (see migration-bags.log)".
- **M6 Report bought tiers.** For every `counts/*.properties` holding `_bought.<Id>=b` with Id in {Cobblestone, OakLog, Wheat, Bone}, log each old bag tier t <= b whose bag moved away, or now lies above `bypass.bagMax`. Example: "`<pkey>` bought Cobblestone III (Small Mining Bag) - that tier has no bag now". No counts file is written.

Expected result on Skyy's world (an untouched 0.2.2 default file): 11 lines removed, 20 tokens added (8 of them appended to existing lines), no hand-edited lines. The start log then says "37 recipe unlock(s)" once SkyySacks 0.8.0 provides the Rare ids.

## 11. Build and deploy notes

- **Scripts.**
  - `tools/sacks_0_8_0_patch.py` generates `build_skyysacks_0.8.0.py` from 0.7.6.
  - `tools/coll_0_2_3_patch.py` generates `build_skyycollections_0.2.3.py` from 0.2.2.
  - Plain `python` builds must end with "assembled ...jar". Lint must show 0 fails.
  - Never `--deploy`. `tools/deploy_set.py` is run only with `--check` by builders. Skyy's pinning and deploy flow stays as HANDOFF section 3 describes.
- **javassist limits apply:** no lambdas, generics, varargs, autoboxing, enhanced-for, inner classes, String switch or try-with-resources; methods before callers; one call per synchronized block; doubled f-string braces.
  - `KnowSync` goes before `SweepTask`.
  - `SackDefs.tierCap` gains a Rare branch (an if-chain, not a String switch).
- **Engine rules hold.** No new ECS system, so the one-registerSystem-per-class rule is unaffected. All inventory, known-recipe and page work runs on the world thread (`SweepTask`, page build and click). Nothing runs on `PlayerReadyEvent`.
- **SkyySacks build checks.**
  - 21 bag JSONs and 5 quality JSONs.
  - Every recipe input exists in `Assets.zip` or is a bag id generated here (bolts include `Ingredient_Bolt_Cindercloth`).
  - Each tiered recipe contains the previous tier's id.
  - `KnowledgeRequired` is true on exactly the 20 tiered recipes and false on the Omni.
  - Default caps are strictly rising.
  - Every quality texture path exists in `Assets.zip` (the SkyyVault check).
  - QualityValue is < 8.
  - Lang has 21 names, 21 descriptions and 5 quality labels.
  - The SkyyGear colour cross-check (3.2).
- **Deploy together** (one round). Mixed versions degrade safely:
  - SkyySacks 0.8.0 with Collections 0.2.2 teaches from the old Cobblestone/OakLog/Wheat/Bone rows, and no Rare bag unlocks.
  - Collections 0.2.3 with Sacks 0.7.6 logs the Rare ids as unknown and skips them, while bags stay free.
- **Never go back to SkyySacks 0.7.x once a Rare or Omni bag exists.** 0.7.x ships no asset for those ids, so the items would be unknown to the server. Add this to HANDOFF's deploy rules when the round is pinned.
- Going back to SkyyCollections 0.2.2 is safe. It reads the migrated file (new ids are just recipe ids) and ignores `bypass.bagMax`.

## 12. Found while reading (fix in the same round unless Skyy says otherwise)

1. **/craft ignores recipe knowledge.** SkyySacks crafts by itself, so the Crafting / Smithing tabs and search list and craft the 19 vanilla `KnowledgeRequired` recipes (Bronze armor, pies, ...) without the player knowing them. Fixed by `recipeAllowed` (5.3) `[SKYY?]`, default yes.
2. **`caps()` trusts any `Skyy_Sack_<X>_<Y>`.** An unknown tier word (for example a 0.8 Rare bag read by a 0.7.6 jar) makes that type "carried" with cap 0, and any word becomes a type. 0.8.0 skips both (5.5).
3. **Saved bag stacks store `"Quality": 5`** (Skyy's `universe/players/<uuid>.json`). Changing the asset quality alone would not change owned bags. Restamp (5.6).
4. **SkyyCollections prints size names** ("Small Mining Bag"). 6.2.
5. **Bolt sources (resolved in 0.7.7).** Bolt of Linen / Silk / Cindercloth come only from the Loombench and from salvaging cloth armor. The Loombench's item `Bench_Loom` has quality Developer, its recipe has no bench requirement and needs 3 Cotton Scraps that no drop table gives; the cloth armor needs those bolts and never drops (VERIFIED `Assets.zip`). So the live 0.7.6 Medium / Large and the first 0.7.7 draft could not be crafted in survival. 0.7.7 uses mob-dropped Linen / Shadoweave / Cindercloth Scraps instead (3.1); the build checks each step material is NPC-dropped. Test T15 now means: a survival player can collect each scrap. Scraps per step (6) = placeholder `[SKYY?]`.
6. **Wheat had no Small Farming Bag row** because Small was free. The ladder gives every type four rows.
7. **Bags are tradeable** (AH default, OPEN-QUESTIONS AH 15). The collection gate covers crafting, not trading (question 7).

## 14. Open questions (with the default this spec uses)

1. **Foraging / Farming / Combat / Smithing collections** = Oak Log / Wheat / Bone Fragments / Light Hide. Alternatives: Stick, Essence of Life, Linen Scraps. Mining = Iron is locked.
2. **One ladder, Normal I / Unique III / Rare V / Legendary VII, for all five bags.** Or per bag (for example Iron one tier earlier if iron feels slow).
3. **Rare cap = 6,720.**
4. **Upgrade materials:** Rare = Unique + 3 Bolt of Silk, Legendary = Rare + 3 Bolt of Cindercloth. Or 6 Silk if Cindercloth is too hard.
5. **Omni** = the five Legendary bags at a Workbench, no gate, no extra catalyst.
6. **Coins may unlock bags up to Unique** (`bypass.bagMax=unique`).
7. **Bags stay tradeable** (AH and /trade), so a traded Legendary skips its collection. SkyBlock makes sacks untradeable. A server can add `Skyy_Sack_*` to `Skyy_Market/blocked.txt` for the AH.
8. **No refund** for past coin purchases whose tier lost its bag; they are listed in `migration-bags.log`.
9. **Fix the vanilla knowledge bypass** in /craft in the same SkyySacks version (yes).
10. **Mythic** tooltip `#aa00aa` (Wynn) and page text `#cc66cc` (readable). Texture frames by hue (Unique gold, Rare purple, Legendary blue, Mythic purple), the same as `research/SkyyGear-Stage1-Spec.md` 2.1. If SkyyGear's build changes it, SkyyGear wins.
11. **One-time [Bags] chat notice** for existing bag users (yes, always shown).
12. **Exploration's "slight boosts"** stay later. Shape when built: a small % on top of every cap from SkyyExploration (for example through a `explore:bagbonus:<uuid>` bridge value). Not in this round; tiers VIII and IX stay free for it and for other prestige rewards.
13. **Free switch placement.** In SkyySacks only (it owns the items and must work alone). SkyyCollections just shows "(free on this server)".
